Ellen —

Thanks — summarised options below and attached a short pricing matrix + a proposed commit schedule for your review (pricing_matrix_v2.pdf; proposed_commit_schedule.xlsx). High level:

1) Term & headline discounts (GPU-equivalent pool pricing, A100-eq buckets):
   - 12 months: baseline rate, ~10% program discount (preferred for teams that want flexibility)
   - 24 months: ~18% discount, recommended if you need predictable unit economics and lower unit-price
   - 36 months: ~25% discount + eligibility for onboarding credit (see notes)

2) Activation windows & staging:
   - Standard start: activation within 30 days of signature
   - Soft-start window: up to 90 days with a staged billing ramp (we invoice 25% of committed capacity until full activation)
   - Delay provision: if activation starts >90 days, we can apply an "activation credit" equal to one month of committed fees (negotiable)

3) Ramp & burst policy:
   - Canary: first 30 days, optional canary at 40–60% of pool with production telemetry hooks.
   - Burst: customers can use up to 2x burst for 7-day rolling windows; bursts draw from shared burst capacity subject to fair-use.
   - Billing: charges billed against reserved commit for reserved usage; burst usage billed at on-demand overage rates.

4) Throughput guarantees & remedies:
   - Commit backed throughput: we size your pool to meet target throughput (tokens/sec) at p95; SLA: 99.5% availability of reserved pool slots.
   - Remedies: service credits tiered to SLA misses (up to 10% of monthly committed invoice), legal to confirm caps.

5) GPU pool sizing examples (rough):
   - Small pool: 6 A100-eq — baseline for low-throughput.
   - Medium pool: 12 A100-eq — typical for mid-size realtime workloads.
   - Large pool: 24+ A100-eq — sustained throughput workloads (preferred for batch-heavy embedding pipelines).

Next steps: if this looks in scope I’ll loop in Marissa (contracts) + Karthik (capacity planning) to draft a formal SOW + DocuSign packet.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
